question: What is the common name of E300?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vitamin C, also known as ascorbic acid, is an essential nutrient for humans.
 
• It is a water-soluble vitamin and a powerful antioxidant.
 
• Vitamin C is vital for the maintenance of healthy skin, blood vessels, bones, and cartilage.
 
• It also aids in the healing of wounds and the absorption of iron from plant-based foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin A**

 
 
• Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin important for vision, immune function, and reproduction.
 
• It also helps the heart, lungs, kidneys, and other organs work properly.
 
• Vitamin A comes in two forms: preformed vitamin A (retinol and retinyl ester) and provitamin A carotenoids.
 
• Sources include dairy products, fish, and meat, especially liver.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin D**
 
 
• Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin that is important for maintaining healthy bones and teeth.
 
• It also supports the immune, brain, and nervous system health.
 
• Vitamin D can be synthesized by the body through exposure to sunlight.
 
• Food sources include fatty fish, beef liver, cheese, and egg yolks.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin B**
 
 
• Vitamin B refers to a group of eight water-soluble vitamins that play important roles in cell metabolism.
 
• These include B1 (thiamine), B2 (riboflavin), B3 (niacin), B5 (pantothenic acid), B6 (pyridoxine), B7 (biotin), B9 (folic acid), and B12 (cobalamin).
 
• Each of these vitamins contributes to different functions, such as energy production and the formation of red blood cells.
 
• Sources include whole grains, meat, eggs, dairy products, seeds and nuts, and dark, leafy vegetables.
